HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

Bachelor's degree in related field
10 years related experience

Familiar with Microsoft Office, estimating and scheduling software, project management software

jobs.title: Sr. Privacy Project Manager
jobs.description:
Our client is seeking a Sr. Privacy Project Manager for a long term, multi-year assignment.

As a seasoned Sr. "Privacy" Project Manager with experience delivering real-world complex Data & Advanced Analytics projects, the person is expected to
Plan, execute, and oversee technology and data platform initiatives by coordinating scope, schedule, resources, budget, and deliverables.
Ensure projects are delivered in alignment with approved objectives, governance standards, and quality expectations while supporting our client's data, analytics, and digital transformation initiatives.

Develop, maintain, and manage project plans, schedules, work breakdown structures, and milestone timelines in alignment with approved scope and objectives. Coordinate project activities across cross-functional teams to support timely and efficient execution of deliverables throughout the project lifecycle.

Lead projects focused on data privacy compliance and regulatory alignment.
Drive privacy assessments, security checkpoints, and compliance reviews as part of project delivery. Partner with Legal, InfoSec, and Data Governance teams to ensure appropriate handling of PII, sensitive data, and regulated datasets. Oversee implementation of privacy controls such as access restrictions, masking, minimization, retention workflows, and audit traceability. Ensure that privacy requirements are incorporated into user stories, backlog items, acceptance criteria, and definition of done.

Facilitate all Agile ceremonies and ensure that both data and privacy requirements are visible, prioritized, and worked through in alignment with sprint goals. Partner with Product Owners to maintain dual-focused backlogs that cover feature delivery, data quality enhancements, compliance tasks, and privacy controls.
Remove blockers—technical, process-related, or privacy-related—to maintain delivery flow. Coach teams to improve Agile maturity while maintaining compliance and governance expectations.

Serve as a central point of coordination between business stakeholders, product owners, technical teams, and leadership. Facilitate project meetings, status reviews, and decision forums, ensuring clear, consistent communication of progress, risks, dependencies, and impacts.

Monitor project scope, schedule, and risk by tracking progress against approved plans and identifying variances. Document, manage, and escalate risks, issues, assumptions, and change requests in accordance with established project governance and escalation protocols.

Track and manage project budgets, forecasts, and resource allocations to ensure alignment with approved funding and staffing plans. Support financial reporting, cost monitoring, and resource planning activities in coordination with leadership and finance partners.

Lead end-to-end planning and delivery of data pipelines, modeling efforts, analytics solutions, dashboards, and data modernization initiatives.
Coordinate cross-functional work across data engineering, BI, data governance, QA, product, and business groups. Ensure strong data governance practices—including metadata accuracy, documentation, lineage, and quality controls—are embedded throughout all projects. Manage dependencies across systems and teams to ensure data solutions integrate cleanly and securely.

Minimum Educational Qualifications
• Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

Minimum Experience
• 7+ years of experience managing projects in technology, data, or digital platform environments that enable large-scale enterprise applications and data platforms.
• Demonstrated experience managing cross-functional teams and delivering projects using structured project management methodologies

Other Job-Specific Skills
• Knowledge of project management methodologies (Waterfall, Agile, Hybrid).
• Experience w/project tracking & reporting tools (e.g., MS Project, Jira, Clarity, or similar).
• Strong organizational, risk management, and issue resolution skills.
• Ability to manage multiple initiatives with competing priorities.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills suitable for executive and technical audiences.

Typical key performance indicators:
• On-time delivery of project milestones and deliverables.
• Adherence to approved scope, schedule, budget, and compliance.
• Accuracy and timeliness of project status reporting.
• Stakeholder satisfaction with project execution and outcomes.
• Effectiveness of risk and issue management.

jobs.description:
Syteline (Infor CloudSuite Industrial) Business Analyst

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Syteline Business Analyst to lead functional design, configuration, testing and deployment of Syteline (Infor CloudSuite Industrial) ERP solutions. The role partners with business stakeholders and technical teams to gather requirements, perform gap analysis, define solutions, manage integrations and support go-live and post-implementation activities to ensure the ERP delivers expected business value.

Key Responsibilities

Collaborate with stakeholders to elicit and document business requirements, use cases, user stories and functional specifications for Syteline implementations and enhancements.
Perform business process analysis, gap analysis and solution design across Procure-to-Pay, Order-to-Cash, Inventory, MRP/Manufacturing, Fixed Assets, HCM/Payroll and Financial modules (GL/AP/AR).
Configure and validate Syteline system settings and support safe customization where needed, ensuring alignment with best practices and governance.
Design, execute and oversee integration and data migration activities including data mapping, ETL processes, EDI, REST/SOAP APIs and middleware coordination.
Develop and execute test plans, test cases and UAT scripts; coordinate integration testing, UAT and defect resolution with technical teams and business users.
Create and maintain implementation artifacts including BRDs, functional specifications, process diagrams (Visio/Lucidchart), training materials and release documentation.
Partner with technical teams on reporting and analytics requirements, supporting SQL/PL/SQL, T-SQL, SSRS, Power BI, Tableau or Crystal Reports delivery where applicable.
Work within Agile (Scrum) and Waterfall project methodologies, using tools such as JIRA, Confluence, HP ALM or TestRail to manage requirements, sprints and defects.

Qualifications

Bachelors degree in Information Systems, Business, Computer Science or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years of hands-on ERP business analysis experience, with strong experience specifically on Syteline (Infor CloudSuite Industrial) implementations preferred.
Proven expertise in requirements gathering, business process analysis, gap analysis, functional specifications, user stories, BRDs and test case creation.
Experience with data migration, ETL, data mapping, master data management and SQL (PL/SQL, T-SQL) for data validation and reporting.
Familiarity with integrations and middleware (APIs, REST, SOAP, EDI, MuleSoft, Dell Boomi, Informatica, Tibco or similar) and experience coordinating integration testing.
Strong reporting and analytics skills (SSRS, Power BI, Tableau, Crystal Reports) and advanced Excel including VBA for analysis and reconciliation.
Preferred: familiarity with other ERP platforms and technologies, including SAP S/4HANA, SAP ECC, SAP, Oracle E-Business Suite, Oracle Fusion/Cloud ERP, PeopleSoft, JD Edwards, Microsoft Dynamics/Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Workday, and ABAP familiarity.
Preferred: experience with procurement, order-to-cash, inventory management, manufacturing/MRP, HCM/payroll, SOX compliance, GDPR and financial modules (GL/AP/AR).

jobs.title: Research Data Analyst 2
jobs.description:
Job Description

Who We Are

The Stanford Graduate School of Education (GSE)
is dedicated to solving education's greatest challenges. Through rigorous research, model training programs and partnerships with educators worldwide, we're pursuing equitable, accessible and effective learning for all. The GSE is a top-ranked school of education, known for its prestigious faculty, rigorous graduate degree programs, and its impact on the quality of education across the world. The GSE is committed to developing leaders in education research, practice and policy. Our community includes over 60 faculty, 400 students, 230 staff, 14,000 alumni and countless individuals from the local and global communities that we work with and impact.

The Educational Opportunity Project (EOP), housed in the Graduate School of Education, is seeking a Research Data Analyst 2. The EOP is dedicated to measuring educational opportunity in every community in America and has built the most comprehensive national database of academic performance in the U.S., the Stanford Education Data Archive (SEDA). This position will support work to expand and improve SEDA through contributing to the development and implementation of new linking and estimation methods, the cleaning and integration of new years of data into SEDA, the release of new metrics in the database, and analyses of the SEDA data.

About The Role

The Research Data Analyst 2 will work closely with the Executive and Faculty Directors of the EOP to develop code to clean, organize, and harmonize data from large longitudinal education datasets; to implement statistical estimation methods; and to analyze data for research publications. This position requires independent work as well as collaboration with the EOP team. Significant experience using Stata, a strong statistical background, and careful attention to detail is critical for this role.

This position is a 1-year fixed term appointment with annual renewal contingent on available funds. The position is based on Stanford University’s main campus. Consideration will be given to a hybrid work schedule (partially onsite and offsite work), subject to operational need. Interested candidates should include a resume and cover letter describing why they are interested in this position at this stage in their career.

The expected pay range for this position is $91,852 to $128,138 per annum.

Areas of Focus

Extract and clean data from a variety of sources, including state departments of education and the federal government, and maintain its accuracy and completeness.
Identify potentially problematic data, make corrections, and eliminate the root cause of data problems.
Build replicable and efficient software code for data cleaning and estimation.
Design and customize reports based upon data in the database.
Create complex charts and databases, perform statistical analyses, and develop graphs and tables for publication and presentation.
Serve as a resource for non-routine inquiries such as requests for statistics.
Create documentation for all code.

What You’ll Bring

We are looking for a Research Data Analyst who brings strong statistical skills, technical precision, and careful judgment to work with considerable independence. You have deep experience in Stata, ideally three or more years, and you’re comfortable managing and analyzing large, complex datasets. You write efficient, replicable code, document it so others can follow it, and design code architectures that hold up as the data grows. A master’s or doctoral degree and familiarity with advanced methods such as hierarchical linear modeling are a plus.

You have experience supporting quantitative social science research and know how to turn messy data into reliable evidence. You take ownership of the full data pipeline: extracting and cleaning data from state and federal sources, spotting problems and fixing their root causes, implementing new estimation methods, and producing charts, tables, and analyses ready for publication. You pay close attention to detail while keeping sight of the larger purpose behind the work: measuring educational opportunity in every community in America. Experience with K-12 or postsecondary education data will help you contribute right away.

Strong collaborative instincts are equally important. You work closely with the Executive and Faculty Directors of the Educational Opportunity Project, communicate clearly about methods and findings, and know which questions you can resolve yourself and which need the team’s input. We value someone who serves as a dependable resource for non-routine requests, enjoys solving hard problems, and brings curiosity, persistence, and pride in producing rigorous, high-quality work.

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Prioritize and extract data from a variety of sources such as notes, survey results, medical reports, and laboratory data, and maintain its accuracy and completeness.
Determine additional data collection and reporting requirements.
Design and customize reports based upon data in the database. Oversee and monitor regulatory compliance for utilization of the data.
Use system reports and analyses to identify potentially problematic data, make corrections, and eliminate root cause for data problems or justify solutions to be implemented by others.
Create complex charts and databases, perform statistical analyses, and develop graphs and tables for publication and presentation.
Serve as a resource for non-routine inquiries such as requests for statistics or surveys.
Test prototype software and participate in approval and release process for new software.
Provide documentation based on audit and reporting criteria to investigators and research staff.

Minimum Education

Bachelor's degree and three years of relevant experience or combination of education and relevant experience.

Minimum Experience

Experience in a quantitative discipline such as economics, finance, statistics or engineering.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Substantial experience with MS Office and analytical programs.
Excellent writing and analytical skills.
Ability to prioritize workload.

At Elroy Air, we build autonomous vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) cargo drones to change the way the world moves goods. Transporting cargo by air is faster and more direct than by land or sea, but it has been prohibitively expensive for medium-size loads. We've set out to expand middle-mile logistics possibilities across multiple sectors, with our sights on a $420Bn global total addressable market for cargo logistics across defense, commercial and rapid response.

We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe that the defense, commercial, and rapid response communities need faster, better logistics solutions. We are seeing increasing demand as customers and prospects respond enthusiastically to the systems we’ve built. As we mature and deploy our offerings, we are looking for people like you: motivated collaborators, enthusiastic about our mission and ready to roll up their sleeves and make a big impact to improve how logistics works around the world. You will play an important role in establishing the Elroy Air Chaparral as the industry standard in this massive market.

We believe diverse perspectives at all levels of the organization are critical to innovation and employee development. This includes but is not limited to gender identity, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender expression, religion, age, ability, parenthood status, veteran status, educational background, citizenship status, or any combination of these characteristics.

$175,000 - $210,000 a year

Role Description

This is a high-ownership, high-impact role for an experienced Technical Program Manager (TPM) with a strong background in complex hardware and software integration. You will drive end-to-end program execution across aircraft subsystems, including propulsion, powertrain, avionics, flight controls, and ground support systems. You will establish program schedules, manage critical path dependencies, mitigate technical risks, and ensure seamless cross-functional delivery from early design and flight test through to production ramp.

Attribute
Details

Title

Senior Technical Program Manager

Location

Byron, CA – hybrid

Level

Senior individual contributor

Scope

End-to-end technical program leadership across hybrid-electric propulsion, avionics, flight test, and system integration.

This role is a hybrid position based out of our Byron office, but on-site presence will naturally fluctuate depending on program milestones and build cycles. As a TPM, you are ultimately responsible for being present on-site to ensure the successful execution, integration, and delivery of hardware builds. During active build, assembly, and integration phases, you can expect to be in our Byron facility up to 4 or 5 days a week to work directly with engineering and shop floor teams. During desk-heavy phases—such as early requirements definition, planning, and documentation—your schedule will lean more flexible, averaging around 2 days on-site per week. Some travel will also be required, including visits to flight test facilities and key partner locations.

What You’ll Do:

Lead Prototype Build Execution & Integration: Serve as the primary program owner responsible for the build, bring-up, and end-to-end integration of our primary test platform housing all powertrain components—driving hardware/software tuning, system integration, and risk de-risking ahead of flight test.
Drive Program Execution: Establish, manage, and track integrated master schedules (IMS) across hardware, software, and systems engineering streams to hit aggressive company flight test and certification milestones.
Manage Technical Risks & Dependencies: Proactively identify critical path risks, system interdependencies, and technical bottlenecks. Facilitate trade studies, risk burn-down strategies, and architectural alignment across cross-functional teams.
Bridge Engineering & Manufacturing: Partner closely with Mechanical, Electrical, Flight Controls, Software, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain engineering teams to ensure seamless progression from prototype build to flight test and production.
Communicate & Align Stakeholders: Lead program reviews, planning, and executive reporting. Communicate schedule status, blocker resolution, and risk metrics clearly to leadership, key external partners, and customers.
Refine TPM Processes: Establish scalable program management best practices, requirement tracking frameworks, change management controls, and reporting dashboards light enough to keep startup velocity while rigorous enough for aerospace safety standards.
Maintain Regulatory & Quality Compliance: Align program milestones with aerospace certification pathways (FAA, Military Airworthiness) and quality standards including AS9100, DO-178C, DO-254, and ITAR/EAR export controls.

Our Ideal Candidate:

6+ years of technical program management experience delivering complex hardware, software, or integrated electro-mechanical systems in aerospace, defense, robotics, automotive, or autonomous systems.
Proven track record managing multi-disciplinary engineering programs through full lifecycle execution—from concept trade studies to flight test and rate production.
Deep technical literacy across hardware engineering, software development lifecycles, systems engineering, and flight test operations.
Mastery of modern program management tools and methodologies (e.g., Jira, Confluence, MS Project, Smartsheet.
Demonstrated ability to influence without authority, lead cross-functional engineering teams, and drive technical consensus in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and risk management capabilities, with a focus on metrics-driven progress tracking.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering (Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Computer Science, Systems) or a related technical discipline.
A scrappy, solutions-oriented professional who thrives in unstructured environments and builds lean, effective processes to maintain momentum.

Bonus Points For:

Experience managing VTOL, UAV, or electric/hybrid-electric aircraft programs.
Familiarity with FAA/civil airworthiness certification processes, ARP4754A, DO-178C, DO-254, and AS9100 standards.
Hands-on experience with flight testing, or flight hardware qualification.
Prior experience scaling technical program management functions within high-growth engineering startups or aerospace primes.

. Minimum qualifications:

5 years of experience in program management.

Experience working with engineering teams.

Preferred qualifications:

5 years of experience managing cross-functional or cross-team projects.
Track record of successfully delivering complex software products, and in-depth knowledge of project management.
Ability to establish systems to continuously improve our business processes, products, or services on an ongoing basis, through measurement of performance, progress, and success metrics.
Exceptional skills influencing and delivering solutions in a highly complex, always changing, and nebulous environment.
Excellent verbal/written communication and problem-solving skills. Outstanding organizational, prioritization, and multitasking skills.

About The Job

A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Technical Program Manager at Google, you’ll use your technical expertise to lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish. You’ll work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify risks, manage project schedules, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. You're equally comfortable explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to executives as you are discussing the technical tradeoffs in product development with engineers.

As a Technical Program Manager with Google Cloud Platform, you lead complex, multi-disciplinary engineering projects using your engineering expertise, with a focus on capacity planning programs and processes. You proactively identify, organize, and lead portfolio activities and stakeholders in order to successfully deliver technical solutions. You scope, phase, and lead ambiguous cross-functional and cross-organizational challenges including delivering downstream change management, alongside your stakeholder team. You ensure alignment of senior cross-functional and cross-organizational stakeholders. You have advanced knowledge of the domain of your program. You also engage in community contributions to improve and sustain our culture and operations making Google a better place to work.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $163000 - $236000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Lead several engineering program management for a fast paced, innovative engineering team. Work hand-in-hand with our cross-organizational engineering, product and business stakeholders to deliver outstanding program outcomes alignment with business priorities.
Identify stakeholders and work with them to strategize, plan, and prioritize objectives and success criteria.
Manage project schedules, identify possible issues and clearly communicate them to project stakeholders and leadership.
Take responsibility for release schedules and milestones, keeping up a high velocity in a fast-paced environment.

jobs.title: Project Manager CBTC/ Car Systems
jobs.description:
In a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities. Imagine Next!

At Parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. Guided by our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. Unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible.

Job Description

Parsons is looking for a Project Manager – CBTC / Car Systems to join our New York Rail & Transit team. In this role, you will lead owner-side delivery of carborne train control and car-systems programs for major transit agencies in the New York region. That includes CBTC retrofits, onboard data communication systems, and vehicle–signal integration on new and existing fleets. You will manage technical oversight, contractor coordination, testing and commissioning, and commercial controls from design review through revenue service and closeout. You'll work alongside owners, CBTC suppliers, railcar manufacturers, and operations and maintenance groups.

What You'll Be Doing

Manage delivery of carborne CBTC and car-systems contracts, including scope, schedule, staff, budget, risk, and the client relationship.
Serve as the owner's main point of contact for field activities. Coordinate test-track and mainline work, track access, and service diversions with operations, car equipment, and labor support groups.
Oversee the inspection, Post-Installation Checkout (static and dynamic PICO), factory acceptance testing, integration testing, and CBTC Operation testing needed to reach revenue service.
Track CBTC software releases through development, validation, and safety validation, Support Technical working groups and safety certification board approvals.
Review contractor submittals, test procedures, and correspondence for compliance with technical specifications and interoperability interface requirements.
Lead technical meetings with CBTC suppliers (Siemens, Hitachi, Alstom, Mitsubishi etc.) and railcar builders to resolve vehicle–train control interface issues, revenue-service incidents, and reliability and availability problems.
Prepare scopes, RFPs, and rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimates for additional work orders. Take part in change and AWO negotiations with clients and contractors.
Review and approve payment milestones, as Resident Engineer when required, and prepare monthly project status reports.
Maintain project risk registers and mitigation plans. Oversee closeout of punch lists, capital spares, and contract deliverables.
Supervise and mentor inspectors, engineers, and assistant project managers.
Support business development and proposals for CBTC, onboard communications, and fleet retrofit pursuits.

What Required Skills You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
10+ years of experience in rail transit systems, including at least 5 years on CBTC or train control projects.
Hands-on experience with carborne CBTC installation, PICO, testing, and commissioning on heavy-rail transit fleets.
Experience managing or overseeing CBTC contractors on owner-side or PMC/CM assignments, including submittal review, payment certification, and change management.
Working knowledge of at least one major CBTC supplier platform.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including chairing multi-party technical meetings and preparing client reports.
Ability to work field and off-hours shifts as testing and track access require.

What Desired Skills You'll Bring

PE license and/or PMP certification.
Experience with NYCT/MTA C&D CBTC programs, including the I2S interoperability requirements.
Experience with onboard data communication systems (DCS), radio, or ATS integration.
Experience with CBTC system safety certification and RAM programs.
Familiarity with IEEE 1474 and CENELEC standards.

Security Clearance Requirement

None

jobs.title: Supply Chain Program Manager II
jobs.description:
Application Close Date

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

The Supply Chain Program Manager (SCPM) is a supply chain owner responsible for converting program demand, design, and schedule into executable sourcing strategies that deliver material on time and on budget. This role operates in an AI-first environment where automation of transactional tasks is encouraged.

The SCPM will be embedded directly with engineering and manufacturing teams, participating in design reviews, trade studies, and production planning from the earliest stages. You will own the end-to-end supplier lifecycle: building bid packages, running competitive source selection events, qualifying new suppliers, negotiating contracts, and driving supplier readiness through PPAP, capability studies, and run-at-rate validation. You will work in a fast-paced environment with a focus on cost-down, dual-sourcing, and cycle time compression.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in ambiguity, moves fast with incomplete information, embraces technology and automation.

Responsibilities

Sourcing & Supplier Management

Build comprehensive bid packages with technical requirements, commercial terms, and evaluation criteria in collaboration with Supply Chain Engineers and Commodity Managers
Support competitive source selection events
Qualify and onboard new suppliers, including facility assessments, capability validation, and contract execution
Drive supplier readiness through PPAP, tooling acceptance, Control Plans, capability studies (Cp/Cpk), and run-at-rate validation to prove suppliers can meet high-rate production demands
Validate supplier capacity to scale from low-rate initial production through high-rate steady-state, ensuring adequate tooling, equipment, shifts, and process capability
Develop and execute dual/tri-source strategies to mitigate risk and drive cost competition
Conduct make/buy/where trade studies in partnership with engineering and manufacturing to support vertical integration decisions
Negotiate contracts, pricing, terms, and remedies with suppliers; manage long-term agreements (LTAs/MSAs) with indexed pricing and capacity commitments

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Reporting

Embed with assigned technical programs
Partner with Supply Chain Engineers on technical readiness and Commodity Managers on commercial strategy
Provide detailed status, risk, and mitigation reporting to program leadership and executive stakeholders
Use data and dashboards (auto-generated by AI agents) to identify trends, predict delays, and drive corrective action

AI-First Operating Model

Define requirements for AI-driven procurement automation: bid package generation, supplier risk screening, PO/ASN reconciliation, and predictive analytics
Supervise automated processes with human-in-the-loop approvals; focus time on strategic decisions and exceptions
Continuously improve templates, workflows, and automation to compress cycle time and eliminate manual work

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree with 4+ years OR Master's degree with 2+ years of supply chain, engineering, or program management experience in manufacturing environments
Exposure to NPI (New Product Introduction) or development programs from design through high-rate production at scale
Experience with First Article Inspection, supplier capability studies, and production readiness validation including run-at-rate assessments
Understanding of high-rate production requirements: takt time, line balancing, capacity validation, and supplier scalability from low-rate to high-rate
Experience building and executing sourcing strategies: competitive events, dual-sourcing, make/buy trades, and total cost analysis
Excellent cross-functional collaboration skills; able to embed with engineering and manufacturing teams and influence
Superior communication skills—able to distill complex supply chain issues into clear executive summaries and recommendations
Strong analytical and quantitative skills; experience with BOMs, MRP/ERP systems, material estimating, cost modeling, and supply chain metrics
Comfort with digital tools, supplier portals, EDI/TMS, and data-driven decision-making; enthusiasm for AI/automation adoption
Self-starter who can define scalable processes, build templates, and operate effectively in a startup-like environment
Willingness to travel (up to 25%) for supplier visits, audits, and on-site problem-solving

Desired Qualifications

Experience in high-rate manufacturing environments with takt-driven planning, JIT principles, and production rates
Experience onboarding and developing new suppliers, including international/global sourcing across multiple regions
Lean Six Sigma training (Green Belt or higher) or equivalent continuous improvement experience
Experience with cost-down strategies: should-cost modeling, learning curves, indexed pricing, and competitive re-bids
Experience working with various commodity types: castings/forgings, machined parts, assemblies, electronics, raw materials, and special processes (welding, heat treat, coatings, NDT)
Background in supplier development, capacity planning, and capital investment in supplier base
Familiarity with export control requirements and global supply chain compliance

Culture Statement

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Export Control Regulations

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Background Check

Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

Benefits

Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

jobs.title: Security Manager LatAm
jobs.description:
Introduction

Welcome to Gallagher - a global community of people who bring bold ideas, deep expertise, and a shared commitment to doing what’s right. We help clients navigate complexity with confidence by empowering businesses, communities, and individuals to thrive. At Gallagher, you’ll find more than a job; you’ll find a culture built on trust, driven by collaboration, and sustained by the belief that we’re better together. Whether you join us in a client-facing role or as part of our brokerage division, our benefits and HR consulting division, or our corporate team, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, make an impact, and be part of something bigger. Experience a workplace where you’re encouraged to be yourself, supported to succeed, and inspired to keep learning. That’s what it means to live The Gallagher Way.

Overview

This role supports Gallagher operations across Latin America. It brings together physical security, employee safety, threat and incident management, emergency preparedness, security intelligence, security technology, vendor oversight, and regional risk reduction.

You’ll help turn global and Americas security strategy into practical local action across a multi country region. That means working across different laws, languages, cultures, infrastructure limits, and threat conditions, while keeping Gallagher standards clear, usable, and consistent. Travel is expected for around 30 to 50 percent of the time, including regular cross border trips.

How You'll Make An Impact

In this role, you’ll run the day to day execution of Gallagher’s Global Safety & Security work across Latin America. You’ll be the main in region contact for security matters, helping country and business leaders make sensible decisions when the risk picture changes. You’ll monitor local conditions such as crime, civil unrest, political issues, natural hazards, transport disruption, and infrastructure problems, then turn that information into practical advice for the business.

Day to day, you’ll carry out physical security reviews, site audits, readiness checks, and country risk assessments. You’ll spot gaps, document vulnerabilities, and follow remediation through to completion. You’ll also support new office openings, moves, closures, consolidations, and acquisitions by helping shape access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management, duress alarms, and other security measures that fit the local environment.

You’ll also play a key part in incident response and crisis coordination. That includes supporting investigations, preserving and translating incident details when needed, joining regional incident and crisis calls, and helping with employee accountability, emergency communications, evacuation, shelter in place, and relocation planning when required. When travel, events, or executive visits involve higher risk, you’ll work with intelligence, travel risk, and executive protection partners to help plan safe and practical support.

Build and maintain country level response plans, escalation paths, emergency contacts, and security records.
Work closely with Human Resources, Legal, Real Estate, Technology, Compliance, Business Continuity, Communications, and local office teams.
Oversee local security vendors and service providers, including performance, compliance, and contract delivery.
Share timely intelligence, incident reports, risk updates, and corrective action tracking with GSS leadership.
Contribute to dashboards, risk registers, leadership updates, and regional program reviews.

About You

Bachelor’s degree in security management, criminal justice, emergency management, business, international relations, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
5 or more years of progressive experience in corporate security, physical security, incident management, law enforcement, military security, emergency management, investigations, intelligence, or a related risk function.
Experience supporting security operations across multiple Latin American countries, cities, or jurisdictions.
Experience carrying out physical security and country risk assessments and turning findings into practical mitigation plans.
Experience coordinating security incidents with business teams, security providers, law enforcement, and emergency services.
Working knowledge of access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management, alarm monitoring, and related security technology.
Experience overseeing contract security providers or other third party security services.
Ability to write concise incident reports, risk assessments, executive summaries, and operational updates in English.
Fluency in Spanish and English.
Preferred portuguese proficiency.
Ability to travel regularly across Latin America and respond to urgent incidents outside normal business hours.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and work across different cultures, legal systems, and business environments.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and related business applications.

jobs.description:
What To Expect

The Security Engineering (SecEng) team is responsible for designing, installing, and maintaining Access Control, Video Surveillance, and Intrusion systems across all Tesla corporate, manufacturing, production, and sales environments. The goal of our team is to ensure all current and future Tesla facilities are equipped with the necessary security systems that are critical for the safety of our employees as well as public visitors. As Tesla continues to grow at a rapid speed, our responsibility to provide and maintain the proper security systems to all new locations continues to increase. Our team is looking for a Project Manager specializing in Physical Security who will be able to lead a high volume of projects across our lines of business simultaneously. This role will report to our North America (NORAM) Security Engineering Program Manager and will support a high volume of fast-moving projects throughout the US, Canada, and Mexico.

As a SecEng project manager, you will be responsible for a broad range of tasks including, but not limited to, design and implementation of security systems for various Tesla locations across NORAM, effective communication with both internal and external parties, and completion of project deliverables prior to strict site opening deadlines. You will be expected to perform with little guidance while still taking the initiative, showing integrity, and operating with a strong sense of urgency, all while managing projects with complex dependencies and tight timelines. You will play a critical role in executing impactful company-wide initiatives as our team strives to continuously improve the effectiveness and resiliency of Tesla security systems across the organization.

The right fit for our team will be a highly motivated, self-sufficient candidate who will be accountable for their work and communicate their goals and objectives effectively to drive key results. They will provide insight and bring creative solutions to potential problems that they may encounter. The ideal candidate must be highly detail-oriented, a lifelong learner, and be able to break through communication barriers in a way that builds trust and creates strong relationships with all our partners. We are looking for someone who will bring the right attitude, the flexibility to adapt to consistent process improvements, and a willingness to get involved to foster alignment with the rest of the SecEng team.

What You'll Do

Responsible for implementing design coordination activities into engineering design packages
Responsible for defining scope of work for installations of security systems including ACS, VSS, and IDS
Accurate coordination, communication, and management of both external vendors and internal Tesla teams
Responsible for developing concise communications and workflows for articulating Security Installation status and on-site conditions
Responsible for as-built verification leveraging Bluebeam software, PlanGrid, Aconex and traditional survey means/methods
Work with Security Engineering, Technical Project Controls, Construction, BIM and Engineering to create process improvements for Coordination, Short Interval Planning, 4D Analysis and other construction-related activities
Expected to work in a fast-paced, high-volume workload environment

What You'll Bring

Project Management Certification such as Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent industry experience
Physical Security Certification such as Physical Security Professional (PSP) or equivalent industry experience
3+ years of hands-on experience managing physical security projects including overseeing the installation of Video Surveillance, Intrusion Detection, and Access Control systems
Experience interfacing with construction and cost control on quantity takeoffs and Work Breakdown Structures
Continuously meeting and exceeding internal and external customer’s expectations
Ownership of a site’s security posture and associated projects through initial site planning, initial build-out, move-add-change projects, site maintenance, and decommissioning

Benefits

Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Triskele Labs is an Australian sovereign, independent, founder owned cybersecurity business, Melbourne CBD based, on a journey to be a leading provider of cybersecurity services done properly, built on purpose, culture and mission. We serve Government, Corporate and Enterprise clients across APRA regulated, highly regulated and public sectors while continuing to support the mid market.

Our services span managed detection and response, digital forensics and incident response, penetration testing and governance, risk and compliance. We build the tools and automations that run those services ourselves, with AI at the centre of how we build, and this role is how that program gets prioritised, delivered and kept moving.

The Technical Program Manager is an AI native role. Triskele Labs builds its internal tools and automations with AI doing the large majority of the work, and this role runs that program the same way: with AI as the primary instrument for analysis, planning, delivery management and reporting, and with a mandate to make the teams it works with faster. It is a forward looking, cutting edge role for someone who already works this way, not a program office role with AI added on.

The role owns the internal build program: the internal tools the DevOps team builds and the automations the Workflow Automation team builds, typically five builds in flight at any time. Working closely with the CTO, the Technical Program Manager decides which tools and automations get built and in what order. From there the role owns the full lifecycle under Triskele Labs' secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC): discovery and planning with the SMEs who own the process, design with the engineers who will build it, agile delivery, testing and UAT, and implementation through to measured adoption.

It is hands on. The Technical Program Manager does the business analysis on every build personally, using AI to map processes, draft and test requirements, model options, generate test plans and interrogate delivery data, and brings that same leverage to the teams. The role exists to speed delivery up by removing ambiguity, decisions and dependencies before they block a build. There are no direct reports; the role leads through the program. Compliance certification and non engineering internal projects sit with a separate Graduate Project Manager, whom this role will mentor on method and tooling.

What You Will Do

Prioritise with the CTO

Maintain, with the CTO, a single prioritised forward plan of internal tooling and automation: what gets built, in what order and why
Bring the analysis behind each decision, built with AI and checked by you: the problem it solves, who it affects, effort against value, dependencies, risk and what AI makes cheap to build that was not before
Turn the agreed priorities into a program plan sequenced across the Workflow Automation and DevOps teams so builds do not compete for the same people
Keep the backlog honest: retire items that no longer earn their place and surface new demand as it arises, including opportunities the teams' own AI tooling opens up and controls or process changes the compliance program needs built

Discover and design with SMEs, AI first

Run discovery with the SMEs who own the process: current state, pain points, target state, constraints and what success will look like, using AI to capture, structure and play back what they tell you
Map the process and write the requirements so the team can build without re-discovery: user stories, data requirements, non functional requirements and acceptance criteria, drafted with AI, tested against the SMEs and refined until they are right
Facilitate design sessions between SMEs and engineers, and use AI to prototype, mock and pressure test options in the room rather than in the next sprint
Agree scope, plan, milestones and resourcing for each build before work starts

Deliver through the SSDLC with AI native teams

Run agile delivery for the Workflow Automation and DevOps teams with their leads, following Triskele Labs' SSDLC: planning, stand ups, reviews, retros, security gates and release readiness
Understand how the teams build with AI, what makes them faster or slower, and shape the program around that rather than around a traditional engineering cadence
Clear the path ahead of the teams: decisions made, SMEs available, dependencies resolved and acceptance criteria agreed before they become blockers
Manage scope, change and dependencies across the five concurrent builds and keep the CTO and SMEs informed of progress, blockers and trade offs
Plan and coordinate testing with the DevOps team, within the SSDLC: acceptance criteria agreed up front, AI generated test cases reviewed and run, UAT with the SMEs, defects triaged and closed
Own implementation and go live: documentation (AI drafted, human checked), training, cutover, communication and a named owner for every tool and automation shipped
Close each build with a review of what was delivered against what was scoped and how much faster it could have gone, and carry the lessons into the next one

Govern, measure and accelerate

Establish light, fit for purpose program governance (templates, stage gates, RAID log, reporting cadence) aligned to the SSDLC, built with AI and designed to speed delivery up rather than add steps in front of it
Produce one internal program report on a regular cadence, generated from live delivery data, with status, risk and delivery metrics that the CTO and ELT use to make decisions
Build and analyse the data behind delivery: dashboards, cycle time and throughput, trend and variance reporting, adoption after go live, and how much of each build AI carried
Keep current on what AI and modern engineering practice make possible, trial new tooling and ways of working, and bring what works into the program and the teams
Mentor a Graduate Project Manager on planning method, AI assisted ways of working and stakeholder management, and bring their projects into the program view where they touch the build teams

Requirements

What we are looking for

Someone who already works AI first. The Technical Program Manager uses AI as the default way of gathering information, doing analysis, writing requirements, planning, making updates, drafting documentation and reporting, and treats a task done without it as the exception that needs a reason. They understand how engineering teams that build primarily with AI actually work, can hold a credible technical conversation with them, and are always looking for the next thing that will make them faster.

This is a multi-faceted role. Strong business analysis underpins all of it: a program manager who cannot analyse a process, write requirements an engineer can build from and read delivery data critically will not succeed in it.

Essential

Demonstrated AI competency: uses AI tooling daily and expertly in their own work (analysis, requirements, documentation, test planning, reporting) and has worked with, or can credibly engage with, engineering teams that build primarily with AI
3 or more years in technical program, project or delivery management
Demonstrated business analysis capability: requirements elicitation and documentation, user stories and acceptance criteria, options analysis, and the judgement to know when a problem needs a process fix rather than a tool
Strong analytical and data skills: comfortable building and interpreting dashboards, cycle time and throughput metrics, trend and variance analysis and adoption tracking; able to interrogate data rather than take it at face value
Technically fluent: able to hold a conversation about architecture, environments, integration, security controls and AI tooling with engineers without translation
Experience shaping and prioritising a tooling, product or automation backlog with a technical executive, and articulating value, effort, dependency and risk trade offs clearly
Experience running the full agile delivery lifecycle with software, platform or automation teams inside a defined secure development lifecycle: discovery and planning with SMEs, design, delivery, testing and UAT, implementation and handover to operation
Proven ability to run concurrent builds with different stakeholders, switch between strategic and detailed work in the same day, and keep each on schedule
Clear written and verbal communication across the full range, from engineering detail to a one-page ELT summary
Influence without authority: a track record of getting commitments and decisions from peers and senior people who do not report to you
A bias to removing friction: comfortable in a lean, fast moving business where governance must be proportionate, templates are built rather than inherited, and the role shapes its own operating model

Desirable

Hands on experience with agentic AI tooling, AI coding assistants or workflow automation platforms (for example n8n, Power Automate or similar), and a view on what is cheap and expensive to automate
Experience with DevOps or platform engineering teams: CI/CD, release management, environments, and the difference between a prototype and a supportable internal tool
Background in cybersecurity, managed services or another operationally intensive technology business where internal tooling directly affects service delivery
Experience mentoring or developing junior project staff
Change management experience: communication planning, training design, adoption measurement and sustaining change after go live
Formal qualifications in project management (PRINCE2, PMP, MSP), business analysis (BABOK or IIBA) or agile delivery (Scrum, SAFe)
Experience selecting and administering project portfolio tooling (for example Asana or Jira) and building automated reporting from it

Benefits

A new and strategic role with autonomy to shape what you build.
This is an AI-native role.
A high-trust, high-accountability culture and direct exposure to executive leadership.
Competitive salary
Investment in training, certification, and conference attendance.
Hybrid working out of our Melbourne office.
Access to Triskele Labs Benefits Program

How To Apply

Applicants should provide a CV and a short cover note addressing the essential criteria, including how they use AI in their own work today. Shortlisted candidates will complete a practical exercise using whatever AI tooling they choose: analyse a short process description, identify the tooling or automation opportunity, and produce a one page plan covering scope, requirements an engineering team could build from, delivery approach under an SSDLC, and how it would be tested and implemented. We will ask how it was produced as well as what it says.

Triskele Labs is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants must have the right to work in Australia; some projects may require the ability to obtain an Australian Government security clearance.

jobs.description:
Introduction

At Gallagher Benefit Services, you’re a trusted partner to organizations navigating some of their most important people decisions. We help clients build better workplaces, where people feel supported, empowered, and inspired to thrive. Whether it’s shaping benefit strategies, designing wellbeing programs, or advising on workforce challenges, the work you do here creates meaningful change for businesses and the people who power them. We’re a community of bold explorers, trusted experts, and compassionate partners; working side by side to solve problems, and shape the future of work. Here, curiosity is encouraged, collaboration is second nature, and your ideas have room to grow. If you’re looking for a place where your contribution matters and where you can help build a better world of work; think of Gallagher.

Overview

At Gallagher, we’re passionate about helping people and organisations thrive. Our Total Rewards platform, Gallagher Guide, empowers employees and members to maximise their compensation and rewards. It’s a user-friendly, integrated technology that supports wellbeing across benefits, financial, and career programmes.

As a Client Project Management Consultant Senior, you’ll play a key role in delivering this innovative solution. You’ll work with clients, technical teams, and business partners to implement and enhance our Total Rewards technology. You’ll lead projects, guide teams, and ensure our solutions meet client needs.

How You'll Make An Impact

Lead cross-functional teams to deliver successful projects and product initiatives.
Configure platform capabilities like authentication, content management, messaging, and data analytics.
Collaborate with clients to understand their needs and propose effective solutions.
Manage multiple projects, ensuring quality, timeliness, and client satisfaction.
Provide strategic insights to improve products and services.
Mentor team members and contribute to their professional growth.

About You

Experienced in project management, with 6–8 years in a similar role.
A strong communicator, both written and verbal.
Skilled in critical thinking, problem-solving, and data analysis.
Organised, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities.
Proficient in Microsoft Office and other digital tools.
A team player who can also work independently.
Comfortable leading client discussions and navigating complex challenges.

If you’re ready to make a difference and grow your career in a dynamic, supportive environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Compensation And Benefits

At Gallagher, we believe supporting our colleagues goes far beyond the role itself. For more information, visit our Benefits page.

Competitive compensation
Comprehensive benefits programs designed to support your well-being
Career development opportunities and ongoing learning
A collaborative, people-first culture with accessible leadership
The opportunity to do meaningful work with global reach and local impact

We will also offer reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process if required, so please let us know .

With over 50 years of business expertise and consistent growth, we are known for continuous innovation for our government customers, in both the US and abroad. Our exceptionally talented team is highly collaborative in spirit and practice, producing Results that Matter. Come work with the best! The Joint, Office of the Secretary of Defense, Interagency Division provides expert support services to a range of customers spanning across the Department of Defense, Federal Civilian, and international markets. JOID provides a diverse portfolio of analytical and programmatic capabilities to help our customers make informed decisions on their most challenging issues.

The Acquisition and Technology Analysis Group within JOID specializes in the application of multi-disciplinary analytic skills to support multiple clients within the Department of War (DoW). These clients include the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (OUSW(R&E)), Office of the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment (OUSW(A&S)), DARPA, the Joint Staff, and USINDOPACOM. We are seeking a passionate and dedicated professional interested in providing technical, data-driven support combined with strategy-informed analysis of defense-related topics. Apply a passion for solving challenging, unstructured, and time-critical problems. Participate in analyses, assessments, and workshops that integrate technical, operational, and programmatic aspects across various elements of the DoW. Support cross-functional, high-performance teams conducting quantitative and qualitative analysis, including wargaming, to inform decision makers at the highest levels of the government, including the Secretary of War, Congress, and the White House. Candidates can expect to manage multiple tasks concurrently, often with constrained timelines. Tasks may be aligned to the individual’s expertise and interests but will often require individuals to rapidly learn and apply new knowledge and skills. Successful candidates will quickly be rewarded with leadership opportunities and direct engagement with external clients and stakeholders.

Active TS/SCI clearance.

Desired

Applying intelligence data on near-peer adversary capabilities.
Assessing the operational impact of planned or conceptual weapon systems.
Analyzing implications of technology policy.
Analyzing DoW acquisition processes.
Supporting DoW wargames, tabletop exercises, or workshops.
Supporting international collaboration efforts.

About Us

Finnegan is more than just a law firm – we are a powerhouse of innovation and strategy growth. We pride ourselves on providing top-tier intellectual property services globally. Our success is rooted in our emphasis on relationships with our clients and each other. We care about every individual, and it is why many professionals have spent their entire careers at Finnegan.

Role Overview

The Business Intelligence Analyst
is responsible for collecting, analyzing, and interpreting business data to support strategic and operational decision-making. This role develops reports, dashboards, and data visualizations that provide actionable insights into financial, operational, and business performance metrics.

Responsibilities

Develops, maintains, and enhances Power BI dashboards, management reports, and analytical tools for firm leadership.
Builds reporting that provides clear visibility into firm, office, practice group, client, matter, and timekeeper performance.
Improves existing reporting through automation, standardization, and elimination of unnecessary manual processes.
Creates dashboards and visualizations that allow leaders to quickly identify trends, exceptions, and areas requiring attention.
Supports ad-hoc reporting.
Performs validation and reconciliation to ensure reports and dashboards are complete and accurate.
Researches discrepancies and works with Finance, IT, and other departments to resolve data issues.
Establishes and maintains consistent business definitions, calculations, and reporting methodologies.
Documents data sources, reporting logic, calculations, and processes. Utilizes the firm's accounting databases to prepare profitability reports, financial forecasts, and other reports requested by management.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Business Analytics, Finance, or a related field
Minimum of three years’ experience in business intelligence, data analysis, or a related role, ideally within a professional services or legal environment
Proficiency in data visualization and analytics tools such as Power BI, Tableau, SQL, Excel, and data modeling techniques; experience with Aderant or similar enterprise financial system preferred
Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Word and Excel; experience with Windows-based word processing, databases, spreadsheets, and document management systems
Familiarity with legal industry software, including billing systems, and document management tools
Understanding of industry metrics, legal service delivery models, and competitive benchmarking
Strong analytical mindset with attention to detail and a passion for solving complex data challenges
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; capable of translating data insights for both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Demonstrates exceptional attention to detail and accuracy; skilled in proofreading with strong grammar skills
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment while meeting tight deadlines
Demonstrated initiative and adaptability; capable of working independently and collaboratively
Strong interpersonal skills; able to interact professionally with attorneys, clients, staff, and external partners
Willingness to work overtime when necessary and contribute positively as a team player on all projects

Join Finnegan where your skills will drive success of one of the world’s leading IP law firms.

jobs.title: Investment Performance & Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Founded in 1988, Morrison is a leading global infrastructure manager, investing across the risk spectrum in both private and listed markets. Our purpose is to invest wisely in ideas that matter. We believe the best investments serve an enduring societal need and have a firm commitment to sustainability.
If you’re passionate about investment markets, performance analytics and using technology to turn complex data into meaningful insight, this is an opportunity to join our Listed Markets team in London.

As the Investment Performance and Data Analyst,
you will play an important role in delivering accurate, timely and insightful performance, attribution and investment reporting across our listed market portfolios. You’ll work closely with portfolio managers and investment teams, while also helping operate and develop GATE, our in-house investment research and reporting platform.

About the Job

Prepare, review and explain portfolio performance, attribution and benchmark-relative outcomes across investment strategies, products and mandates.
Maintain and enhance performance measurement processes, including return calculations, attribution models, benchmark mapping and reporting controls.
Investigate performance anomalies, data quality issues and reconciliation breaks, working across investment, operations, distribution and data providers to resolve issues.
Support monthly, quarterly and ad hoc investment reporting for portfolio managers, boards, clients, consultants, platforms and distribution teams.
Operate and develop GATE, including its automated data and reporting processes, data connectors, dashboards and reporting templates.
Review AI-assisted analysis and reporting for accuracy and help improve the quality of its outputs.
Use Python and SQL to maintain, test and enhance investment data and reporting processes.
Contribute to investment governance, performance reviews, committee papers, due diligence and regulatory or compliance reporting.
Help improve and automate processes while maintaining strong controls, documentation and audit trails.

About You

You’re analytically strong, highly detail-oriented and genuinely interested in understanding what drives investment performance. You’re equally comfortable working with investment concepts and getting into the underlying data and technology.
Ideally, you’ll bring:
A tertiary qualification in finance, commerce, economics, accounting, mathematics, statistics, data analytics, computer science or a related discipline.
5+ years’ experience in investment performance, attribution, investment reporting, investment data or a related investment management role.
A sound understanding of investment markets, benchmarks, portfolio construction, performance measurement and attribution.
Working knowledge of Python and SQL, including the ability to read, test and maintain code.
Advanced Excel capability.
Strong problem-solving skills and an interest in automation, data quality and building scalable reporting processes.
The ability to translate complex technical analysis into clear, practical insights for investment, governance and client-facing stakeholders.
Experience with tools such as FactSet PA, Git, APIs, performance systems or market data platforms would be advantageous.
CFA, CIPM, CA, CPA, FRM or a postgraduate finance qualification would also be highly regarded.

This role requires presence and availability during trading hours. We recognise the importance of flexibility and will consider arrangements such as adjusted start and finish times and hybrid working, subject to business needs and the requirements of the role.

Why Morrison?

This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to sit at the intersection of investments, data and technology. Rather than simply producing performance reports, you’ll have the opportunity to understand what is driving investment outcomes, work closely with portfolio managers and contribute to the continued development of the technology and processes behind our investment decision-making.
If you’re excited by the opportunity to combine investment knowledge, analytical thinking and technology in a role with genuine exposure to the investment process, we’d love to hear from you.

Morrison is an equal opportunity employer, and we encourage people of all backgrounds to apply. Please let us know if you require any support or adjustments during the recruitment process.

Morrison works with selected recruitment partners under formal agreements. We do not accept unsolicited resumes, and any such submissions will not be considered or give rise to any fee.

new_jobs.description:
Who we are

We’re a global, midsize CRO that pushes boundaries, innovates and invents because the path to a cure for the world’s most persistent diseases is not paved by those who play it safe. It is built by those who take pioneering, creative approaches and implement them with quality and excellence.

We are Worldwide Clinical Trials, and we are a global team of over 3,500+ experts, bright thinkers, dreamers and doers and, together, we are changing the way the world experiences CROs – in the best possible way.

Our mission is to work with passion and purpose every day to improve lives and we are looking for others who value this same pursuit.

Why Worldwide

We believe everyone plays an important role in making a world of difference for patients and their caregivers. From our hands-on, accessible leaders, to our cohesive and supportive teams, we are committed to enabling professionals from all backgrounds and experiences to succeed. We prioritize cultivating a diverse and inclusive environment that continues to promote collaboration and creativity. We are proud to be a workplace where people thrive by being themselves and are inspired to do their best work every day. Join us!

What The Project Management Department Does At Worldwide

Worldwide Clinical Trials Project management is the perfect blend of operational rigor and therapeutic expertise, with a client-focused approach. Our Global Project Leads (GPLs) and Clinical Project Managers (CPMs) expertly guide our project teams to deliver with high quality, focusing on “doing it right the first time”.

The Project Management team is engaged in all aspects of the trial collaborating with scientific and therapeutic leadership, coordinating across project teams, and providing flexible, innovative and proactive solutions. At Worldwide, you will be dedicated to a specific therapeutic area which will not only give you an opportunity to develop in depth global operational expertise, but also benefit from exceptional scientific and medical background that our experts bring.

What You Will Do

Senior Project Manager (SPM) is responsible for the overall coordination and management of clinical trials from start-up through closeout activities.
Directs the technical, financial and operational aspects of the projects -- thus securing the successful completion of clinical trials. 
Works with major functional area leads to identify and evaluate fundamental issues on the project, interpret data on complex issues, make good business decisions and ensure solutions are implemented.
Works to ensure that all project deliverables meet the customer’s time/quality/cost expectations
The SPM, with support from the Project Management Directors, working in collaboration with other functional area leads, is accountable for ensuring that all project deliverables meet the customer/contract expectations.

What You Will Bring To The Role

High level of responsibility and accountability in all tasks.
Communication skills.
Ability to effectively perform in demanding situations.
Thorough knowledge of project management processes with a solid understanding of how to craft and manage a project budge.
Can demonstrate experience of successfully managing and/or leading multidisciplinary project teams.

Your Experience

6-7 years' industry experience with a minimum of 5 years in a Clinical Project Management role, within a CRO setting.
Oncology experience in a PM role is required.
University/College degree, within Life Science is preferred.
Ability to travel when needed

At Worldwide Clinical Trials, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace by providing transparent compensation.

The salary range for this position is annually (For hourly paid positions, the stated salary range reflects hourly rates):

United States of America - $128,500.00 - $254,500.00

The salary range provided is intended to give candidates an understanding of potential earnings. Compensation will fall within the provided range, and it not a guarantee of exact salary. The final salary will be determined based on relevant experience, performance, education, and internal equity. In addition to base salary, we offer a competitive benefits package depending on location. We ensure pay equity and transparency and comply with all applicable labor laws. Salary information will be discussed during the interview process, and we encourage candidates to inquire about compensation at any stage.

We love knowing that someone is going to have a better life because of the work we do.
