new_jobs.title: Security Manager LatAm
new_jobs.description:
Introduction

Welcome to Gallagher - a global community of people who bring bold ideas, deep expertise, and a shared commitment to doing what’s right. We help clients navigate complexity with confidence by empowering businesses, communities, and individuals to thrive. At Gallagher, you’ll find more than a job; you’ll find a culture built on trust, driven by collaboration, and sustained by the belief that we’re better together. Whether you join us in a client-facing role or as part of our brokerage division, our benefits and HR consulting division, or our corporate team, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, make an impact, and be part of something bigger. Experience a workplace where you’re encouraged to be yourself, supported to succeed, and inspired to keep learning. That’s what it means to live The Gallagher Way.

Overview

This role supports Gallagher operations across Latin America. It brings together physical security, employee safety, threat and incident management, emergency preparedness, security intelligence, security technology, vendor oversight, and regional risk reduction.

You’ll help turn global and Americas security strategy into practical local action across a multi country region. That means working across different laws, languages, cultures, infrastructure limits, and threat conditions, while keeping Gallagher standards clear, usable, and consistent. Travel is expected for around 30 to 50 percent of the time, including regular cross border trips.

How You'll Make An Impact

In this role, you’ll run the day to day execution of Gallagher’s Global Safety & Security work across Latin America. You’ll be the main in region contact for security matters, helping country and business leaders make sensible decisions when the risk picture changes. You’ll monitor local conditions such as crime, civil unrest, political issues, natural hazards, transport disruption, and infrastructure problems, then turn that information into practical advice for the business.

Day to day, you’ll carry out physical security reviews, site audits, readiness checks, and country risk assessments. You’ll spot gaps, document vulnerabilities, and follow remediation through to completion. You’ll also support new office openings, moves, closures, consolidations, and acquisitions by helping shape access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management, duress alarms, and other security measures that fit the local environment.

You’ll also play a key part in incident response and crisis coordination. That includes supporting investigations, preserving and translating incident details when needed, joining regional incident and crisis calls, and helping with employee accountability, emergency communications, evacuation, shelter in place, and relocation planning when required. When travel, events, or executive visits involve higher risk, you’ll work with intelligence, travel risk, and executive protection partners to help plan safe and practical support.

Build and maintain country level response plans, escalation paths, emergency contacts, and security records.
Work closely with Human Resources, Legal, Real Estate, Technology, Compliance, Business Continuity, Communications, and local office teams.
Oversee local security vendors and service providers, including performance, compliance, and contract delivery.
Share timely intelligence, incident reports, risk updates, and corrective action tracking with GSS leadership.
Contribute to dashboards, risk registers, leadership updates, and regional program reviews.

About You

Bachelor’s degree in security management, criminal justice, emergency management, business, international relations, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
5 or more years of progressive experience in corporate security, physical security, incident management, law enforcement, military security, emergency management, investigations, intelligence, or a related risk function.
Experience supporting security operations across multiple Latin American countries, cities, or jurisdictions.
Experience carrying out physical security and country risk assessments and turning findings into practical mitigation plans.
Experience coordinating security incidents with business teams, security providers, law enforcement, and emergency services.
Working knowledge of access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management, alarm monitoring, and related security technology.
Experience overseeing contract security providers or other third party security services.
Ability to write concise incident reports, risk assessments, executive summaries, and operational updates in English.
Fluency in Spanish and English.
Preferred portuguese proficiency.
Ability to travel regularly across Latin America and respond to urgent incidents outside normal business hours.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and work across different cultures, legal systems, and business environments.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and related business applications.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Triskele Labs is an Australian sovereign, independent, founder owned cybersecurity business, Melbourne CBD based, on a journey to be a leading provider of cybersecurity services done properly, built on purpose, culture and mission. We serve Government, Corporate and Enterprise clients across APRA regulated, highly regulated and public sectors while continuing to support the mid market.

Our services span managed detection and response, digital forensics and incident response, penetration testing and governance, risk and compliance. We build the tools and automations that run those services ourselves, with AI at the centre of how we build, and this role is how that program gets prioritised, delivered and kept moving.

The Technical Program Manager is an AI native role. Triskele Labs builds its internal tools and automations with AI doing the large majority of the work, and this role runs that program the same way: with AI as the primary instrument for analysis, planning, delivery management and reporting, and with a mandate to make the teams it works with faster. It is a forward looking, cutting edge role for someone who already works this way, not a program office role with AI added on.

The role owns the internal build program: the internal tools the DevOps team builds and the automations the Workflow Automation team builds, typically five builds in flight at any time. Working closely with the CTO, the Technical Program Manager decides which tools and automations get built and in what order. From there the role owns the full lifecycle under Triskele Labs' secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC): discovery and planning with the SMEs who own the process, design with the engineers who will build it, agile delivery, testing and UAT, and implementation through to measured adoption.

It is hands on. The Technical Program Manager does the business analysis on every build personally, using AI to map processes, draft and test requirements, model options, generate test plans and interrogate delivery data, and brings that same leverage to the teams. The role exists to speed delivery up by removing ambiguity, decisions and dependencies before they block a build. There are no direct reports; the role leads through the program. Compliance certification and non engineering internal projects sit with a separate Graduate Project Manager, whom this role will mentor on method and tooling.

What You Will Do

Prioritise with the CTO

Maintain, with the CTO, a single prioritised forward plan of internal tooling and automation: what gets built, in what order and why
Bring the analysis behind each decision, built with AI and checked by you: the problem it solves, who it affects, effort against value, dependencies, risk and what AI makes cheap to build that was not before
Turn the agreed priorities into a program plan sequenced across the Workflow Automation and DevOps teams so builds do not compete for the same people
Keep the backlog honest: retire items that no longer earn their place and surface new demand as it arises, including opportunities the teams' own AI tooling opens up and controls or process changes the compliance program needs built

Discover and design with SMEs, AI first

Run discovery with the SMEs who own the process: current state, pain points, target state, constraints and what success will look like, using AI to capture, structure and play back what they tell you
Map the process and write the requirements so the team can build without re-discovery: user stories, data requirements, non functional requirements and acceptance criteria, drafted with AI, tested against the SMEs and refined until they are right
Facilitate design sessions between SMEs and engineers, and use AI to prototype, mock and pressure test options in the room rather than in the next sprint
Agree scope, plan, milestones and resourcing for each build before work starts

Deliver through the SSDLC with AI native teams

Run agile delivery for the Workflow Automation and DevOps teams with their leads, following Triskele Labs' SSDLC: planning, stand ups, reviews, retros, security gates and release readiness
Understand how the teams build with AI, what makes them faster or slower, and shape the program around that rather than around a traditional engineering cadence
Clear the path ahead of the teams: decisions made, SMEs available, dependencies resolved and acceptance criteria agreed before they become blockers
Manage scope, change and dependencies across the five concurrent builds and keep the CTO and SMEs informed of progress, blockers and trade offs
Plan and coordinate testing with the DevOps team, within the SSDLC: acceptance criteria agreed up front, AI generated test cases reviewed and run, UAT with the SMEs, defects triaged and closed
Own implementation and go live: documentation (AI drafted, human checked), training, cutover, communication and a named owner for every tool and automation shipped
Close each build with a review of what was delivered against what was scoped and how much faster it could have gone, and carry the lessons into the next one

Govern, measure and accelerate

Establish light, fit for purpose program governance (templates, stage gates, RAID log, reporting cadence) aligned to the SSDLC, built with AI and designed to speed delivery up rather than add steps in front of it
Produce one internal program report on a regular cadence, generated from live delivery data, with status, risk and delivery metrics that the CTO and ELT use to make decisions
Build and analyse the data behind delivery: dashboards, cycle time and throughput, trend and variance reporting, adoption after go live, and how much of each build AI carried
Keep current on what AI and modern engineering practice make possible, trial new tooling and ways of working, and bring what works into the program and the teams
Mentor a Graduate Project Manager on planning method, AI assisted ways of working and stakeholder management, and bring their projects into the program view where they touch the build teams

Requirements

What we are looking for

Someone who already works AI first. The Technical Program Manager uses AI as the default way of gathering information, doing analysis, writing requirements, planning, making updates, drafting documentation and reporting, and treats a task done without it as the exception that needs a reason. They understand how engineering teams that build primarily with AI actually work, can hold a credible technical conversation with them, and are always looking for the next thing that will make them faster.

This is a multi-faceted role. Strong business analysis underpins all of it: a program manager who cannot analyse a process, write requirements an engineer can build from and read delivery data critically will not succeed in it.

Essential

Demonstrated AI competency: uses AI tooling daily and expertly in their own work (analysis, requirements, documentation, test planning, reporting) and has worked with, or can credibly engage with, engineering teams that build primarily with AI
3 or more years in technical program, project or delivery management
Demonstrated business analysis capability: requirements elicitation and documentation, user stories and acceptance criteria, options analysis, and the judgement to know when a problem needs a process fix rather than a tool
Strong analytical and data skills: comfortable building and interpreting dashboards, cycle time and throughput metrics, trend and variance analysis and adoption tracking; able to interrogate data rather than take it at face value
Technically fluent: able to hold a conversation about architecture, environments, integration, security controls and AI tooling with engineers without translation
Experience shaping and prioritising a tooling, product or automation backlog with a technical executive, and articulating value, effort, dependency and risk trade offs clearly
Experience running the full agile delivery lifecycle with software, platform or automation teams inside a defined secure development lifecycle: discovery and planning with SMEs, design, delivery, testing and UAT, implementation and handover to operation
Proven ability to run concurrent builds with different stakeholders, switch between strategic and detailed work in the same day, and keep each on schedule
Clear written and verbal communication across the full range, from engineering detail to a one-page ELT summary
Influence without authority: a track record of getting commitments and decisions from peers and senior people who do not report to you
A bias to removing friction: comfortable in a lean, fast moving business where governance must be proportionate, templates are built rather than inherited, and the role shapes its own operating model

Desirable

Hands on experience with agentic AI tooling, AI coding assistants or workflow automation platforms (for example n8n, Power Automate or similar), and a view on what is cheap and expensive to automate
Experience with DevOps or platform engineering teams: CI/CD, release management, environments, and the difference between a prototype and a supportable internal tool
Background in cybersecurity, managed services or another operationally intensive technology business where internal tooling directly affects service delivery
Experience mentoring or developing junior project staff
Change management experience: communication planning, training design, adoption measurement and sustaining change after go live
Formal qualifications in project management (PRINCE2, PMP, MSP), business analysis (BABOK or IIBA) or agile delivery (Scrum, SAFe)
Experience selecting and administering project portfolio tooling (for example Asana or Jira) and building automated reporting from it

Benefits

A new and strategic role with autonomy to shape what you build.
This is an AI-native role.
A high-trust, high-accountability culture and direct exposure to executive leadership.
Competitive salary
Investment in training, certification, and conference attendance.
Hybrid working out of our Melbourne office.
Access to Triskele Labs Benefits Program

How To Apply

Applicants should provide a CV and a short cover note addressing the essential criteria, including how they use AI in their own work today. Shortlisted candidates will complete a practical exercise using whatever AI tooling they choose: analyse a short process description, identify the tooling or automation opportunity, and produce a one page plan covering scope, requirements an engineering team could build from, delivery approach under an SSDLC, and how it would be tested and implemented. We will ask how it was produced as well as what it says.

Triskele Labs is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants must have the right to work in Australia; some projects may require the ability to obtain an Australian Government security clearance.

We’re looking for an Operations Project Manager
to help lead transformer service projects across critical job sites throughout the U.S. In this role, you’ll oversee daily field operations and crew performance for 2–3 transformer service teams, ensuring projects stay on track, meet safety standards, and deliver high-quality results. This is a great opportunity to take ownership of transformer service delivery while mentoring crews and collaborating with project leadership.

What You’ll Do

Manage 2–3 transformer field crews, supporting scheduling, performance, and development across multiple active job sites
Collaborate with the Regional Manager on project scope, scheduling, crew assignments, quoting, and planning
Conduct field visits to verify safety, crew performance, and project quality; inspect job sites for equipment care and compliance
Coach Crew Supervisors on delegation, scheduling, and productivity improvement
Review and approve timesheets and documentation, ensuring timely submission and accuracy
Oversee job documentation, including reports, JSAs, test results, and change orders; ensure proper upload to internal systems
Guide crews through tasks such as component installation, re-gasketing, vacuum and pressure testing, and transformer oil processing
Support transformer testing (Megger, TTR, Power Factor, SFRA, etc.) and escalate abnormal findings to SMEs
Troubleshoot field issues, including vacuum/pressure loss, dry-air systems, oil processor malfunctions, or wiring errors
Coordinate with SMEs on troubleshooting plans and share knowledge across crews
Promote a culture of safety, compliance, and continuous improvement

Experience We’re Looking For

5–10 years of transformer service experience, including testing, assembly, or oil processing
Mechanical Engineering preferred
NETA Level II, III, or IV certification and/or PMP certification preferred
Class A CDL, OSHA certification, or TWIC card is a plus
Strong Microsoft Office and computer skills
Familiarity with transformer OEMs, power industry customers, and EPC workflows
Ability to read scopes, schematics, diagrams, and nameplates
Understanding of field disposal procedures and environmental standards
Excellent organization, leadership, and communication skills

Additional Requirements

High school diploma or GED
Must be able to travel up to 80%, including nights and weekends
Must complete annual safety training, which may require out-of-state travel
Must successfully complete a background check and pre-employment/random drug tests
Valid driver’s license

Bonus Points For

Completion of a trade school program, technical college, associate degree, or skilled trade certification in welding or a related field
Prior field leadership or project management in transformer or power equipment service
Experience with transformer assembly, LTCs, and reconditioning for various OEMs
Advanced transformer test, troubleshooting, and report analysis skills
Familiarity with SharePoint or job-tracking tools
Background in field crew development or hands-on training

Why Join RMS Energy

Systems Planning and Analysis, Inc. (SPA) delivers high-impact, technical solutions to complex national security issues. With over 50 years of business expertise and consistent growth, we are known for continuous innovation for our government customers, in both the US and abroad. The Joint, Office of the Secretary of Defense, Interagency Division provides expert support services to a range of customers spanning across the Department of Defense, Federal Civilian, and international markets. JOID provides a diverse portfolio of analytical and programmatic capabilities to help our customers make informed decisions on their most challenging issues.

The Acquisition and Technology Analysis Group within JOID specializes in the application of multi-disciplinary analytic skills to support multiple clients within the Department of War (DoW). These clients include the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (OUSW(R&E)), Office of the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment (OUSW(A&S)), DARPA, the Joint Staff, and USINDOPACOM. SPA provides critical decision support to enabling and executing a strategy of technological superiority and enabling the delivery and sustainment of secure, resilient, and preeminent capabilities to the warfighter quickly and cost effectively. Our team of experienced military, technical, and operations research analysts is skilled in evaluating military problems, identifying the driving factors, devising innovative approaches, collecting applicable data, developing necessary software tools, and performing thorough and timely assessments to inform technology and acquisition governance decisions to ensure U.S. military forces retain military superiority in the future.

We have an immediate need for an early-career professional to perform duties as a Jr. Military Operations Analyst, providing onsite support out of Alexandria, VA. This need welcomes disciplines in operations research analysis, intelligence analysis, or science and technology analysis.

Responsibilities

We are seeking a passionate and dedicated professional interested in providing technical, data-driven support combined with strategy-informed analysis of defense-related topics. Apply a passion for solving challenging, unstructured, and time-critical problems. Participate in analyses, assessments, and workshops that integrate technical, operational, and programmatic aspects across various elements of the DoW. Support cross-functional, high-performance teams conducting quantitative and qualitative analysis, including wargaming, to inform decision makers at the highest levels of the government, including the Secretary of War, Congress, and the White House. Candidates can expect to manage multiple tasks concurrently, often with constrained timelines. Successful candidates will quickly be rewarded with leadership opportunities and direct engagement with external clients and stakeholders.

Active TS/SCI clearance.

Master’s degree.

Applying intelligence data on near-peer adversary capabilities.

Founded in 1988, Morrison is a leading global infrastructure manager, investing across the risk spectrum in both private and listed markets. Our purpose is to invest wisely in ideas that matter. We believe the best investments serve an enduring societal need and have a firm commitment to sustainability.
If you’re passionate about investment markets, performance analytics and using technology to turn complex data into meaningful insight, this is an opportunity to join our Listed Markets team in London.

As the Investment Performance and Data Analyst,
you will play an important role in delivering accurate, timely and insightful performance, attribution and investment reporting across our listed market portfolios. You’ll work closely with portfolio managers and investment teams, while also helping operate and develop GATE, our in-house investment research and reporting platform.

About the Job

Prepare, review and explain portfolio performance, attribution and benchmark-relative outcomes across investment strategies, products and mandates.
Maintain and enhance performance measurement processes, including return calculations, attribution models, benchmark mapping and reporting controls.
Investigate performance anomalies, data quality issues and reconciliation breaks, working across investment, operations, distribution and data providers to resolve issues.
Support monthly, quarterly and ad hoc investment reporting for portfolio managers, boards, clients, consultants, platforms and distribution teams.
Operate and develop GATE, including its automated data and reporting processes, data connectors, dashboards and reporting templates.
Review AI-assisted analysis and reporting for accuracy and help improve the quality of its outputs.
Use Python and SQL to maintain, test and enhance investment data and reporting processes.
Contribute to investment governance, performance reviews, committee papers, due diligence and regulatory or compliance reporting.
Help improve and automate processes while maintaining strong controls, documentation and audit trails.

About You

You’re analytically strong, highly detail-oriented and genuinely interested in understanding what drives investment performance. You’re equally comfortable working with investment concepts and getting into the underlying data and technology.
Ideally, you’ll bring:
A tertiary qualification in finance, commerce, economics, accounting, mathematics, statistics, data analytics, computer science or a related discipline.
5+ years’ experience in investment performance, attribution, investment reporting, investment data or a related investment management role.
A sound understanding of investment markets, benchmarks, portfolio construction, performance measurement and attribution.
Working knowledge of Python and SQL, including the ability to read, test and maintain code.
Advanced Excel capability.
Strong problem-solving skills and an interest in automation, data quality and building scalable reporting processes.
The ability to translate complex technical analysis into clear, practical insights for investment, governance and client-facing stakeholders.
Experience with tools such as FactSet PA, Git, APIs, performance systems or market data platforms would be advantageous.
CFA, CIPM, CA, CPA, FRM or a postgraduate finance qualification would also be highly regarded.

This role requires presence and availability during trading hours. We recognise the importance of flexibility and will consider arrangements such as adjusted start and finish times and hybrid working, subject to business needs and the requirements of the role.

Why Morrison?

This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to sit at the intersection of investments, data and technology. Rather than simply producing performance reports, you’ll have the opportunity to understand what is driving investment outcomes, work closely with portfolio managers and contribute to the continued development of the technology and processes behind our investment decision-making.
If you’re excited by the opportunity to combine investment knowledge, analytical thinking and technology in a role with genuine exposure to the investment process, we’d love to hear from you.

Morrison is an equal opportunity employer, and we encourage people of all backgrounds to apply. Please let us know if you require any support or adjustments during the recruitment process.
